from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider 2D circles and 3D spheres.",
            "Generalize to n dimensions using the Pythagorean theorem.",
            "This leads to the hypersphere definition.",
            "Observe the transition into 4D space.",
            "We visualize the hidden 4D structure."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Dimensional Leap", lecture_lines)
        
        # Color definitions
        colors = [BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(square, 'B2', 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(square))
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Transform(square, cube))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        # 4D hypercube wireframe (tesseract)
        tesseract = VGroup(*[Cube(side_length=1.0, stroke_width=1, color=ORANGE) for _ in range(2)])
        tesseract[1].shift(0.2 * RIGHT + 0.2 * UP)
        self.place_in_area(tesseract, 'D2', 'E4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(tesseract))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        dot = Dot(color=GOLD, radius=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.play(dot.animate.scale(2).set_color(GOLD))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = ["High dimensions exhibit concentration of measure.", "Volume collects in a thin surface shell.", "The interior effectively becomes empty."]
        self.setup_layout("The Concentration of Measure", lines)
        
        # Setup Animation Elements
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.03, color=WHITE) for _ in range(50)])
        for dot in dots:
            dot.move_to(np.array([2.5 + np.random.uniform(-1, 1), 0 + np.random.uniform(-1, 1), 0]))
            
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.exp(- (x)**2 / 0.2), x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dots), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(curve, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(curve), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            dots.animate.move_to(self.grid['E4']),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED)
        )

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):

            "Hyperspheres are concentrated at the surface."
        ])
        
        # Elements

        vol_label = Text("Volume Paradox", color=WHITE)

            self.place_at_grid(vol_label, 'C5'),
            self.place_at_grid(surf_label, 'E6')
        ]

        self.play(objs[0].animate.scale(3), labels[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(objs[1].animate.scale(3), labels[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

outline.topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D
outline.target_audience: University students (STEM majors with basic calculus/linear algebra)

sections.title: Introduction: The Dimensional Leap
sections.content: Define an n-sphere. Use a 2D circle (x²+y²=r²) and a 3D sphere (x²+y²+z²=r²) as the foundation, then generalize to n-dimensions using the Pythagorean theorem sum formula.
sections.example: Visual animation: A point 'growing' into a line, then a square, then a cube, then transitioning into the hidden 'shadow' of a 4D hypersphere (tesseract).

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Volume Paradox
sections.content: Explain that as the number of dimensions 'n' increases, the volume of a unit sphere actually tends toward zero. Introduce the Gamma function as the tool for calculating n-dimensional volume.
sections.example: An animation of a 'Blob the Robot' trying to fit a unit sphere into a unit cube; as dimensions increase, the sphere shrinks into the center, leaving almost all the 'cube' volume in the corners.

sections.title: The Concentration of Measure
sections.content: Discuss the 'Spiky Sphere' phenomenon. In high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere is located in a thin shell near the surface and near the equator.
sections.example: Visual: An orange being peeled. In 2D, the peel is a line; in 3D, it's a surface. In 100D, almost the entire 'mass' of the fruit is concentrated in the peel, with the center being effectively 'hollow'.

sections.title: Real-World Application: High-Dimensional Data
sections.content: Connect the theory to Machine Learning. Explain that data points in high-dimensional feature spaces (like pixels in an image or neural network weights) behave like points on a high-dimensional sphere.
sections.example: A 'Data Explorer' character organizing thousands of animal photos; the system maps each animal as a vector on a hypersphere to calculate similarity (cosine similarity).

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap the three core takeaways: 1. Generalization of coordinates, 2. Volume decay in high dimensions, 3. The surface-heavy nature of hyperspheres.
sections.example: A final 5-second zoom-out animation showing a 3D sphere expanding into a complex, shimmering multidimensional lattice, symbolizing the 'curse and blessing of dimensionality'.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The square animation occupies the same column as the lecture text, leading to potential visual obstruction. Fix: Line 63: self.place_in_area(square, 'D2', 'E3', scale_factor=0.6) (line=63, object=square)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The tesseract animation overlaps with the square, cluttering the central workspace. Fix: Line 82: self.place_in_area(tesseract, 'C4', 'D5', scale_factor=0.7) (line=82, object=tesseract)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The dot is floating without a clear association to the new positions of the primary shapes. Fix: Line 89: self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C5', scale_factor=1.0) (line=89, object=dot)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The Gamma function formula overlaps with the sphere and cube elements vertically, causing visual clutter. Fix: Line 75: self.place_at_grid(gamma_text, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0) (line=75, object=gamma_text)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The sphere and cube are currently sharing the same anchor (C3), resulting in poor visual separation. Fix: Line 64: self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C2', scale_factor=0.6); Line 80: self.place_at_grid(cube_rect, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6) (line=64, object=circle, cube_rect)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The corner indicators are positioned too close to the central animation, creating a crowded appearance. Fix: Line 86-89: self.place_at_grid(corners, 'A1', scale_factor=0.4); self.place_at_grid(corners, 'A5', scale_factor=0.4); self.place_at_grid(corners, 'E1', scale_factor=0.4); self.place_at_grid(corners, 'E5', scale_factor=0.4) (line=86, object=corners)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The animation curve is positioned too close to the left-side text area, creating visual clutter. Fix: Line 62: self.place_at_grid(curve, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6) (line=62, object=curve)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The scatter plot points are positioned in the center, causing significant overlap with the left-side lecture notes. Fix: self.place_in_area(scatter_plot, 'D3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=62, object=scatter_plot)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The animation curve lacks a descriptive label, leading to ambiguity in the educational context. Fix: self.place_at_grid(Label('Distribution'), 'B4', scale_factor=0.5) (line=62, object=curve)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The matrix and outlier are horizontally centered, creating an obstruction overlap with the lecture notes on the left. Fix: Line 64: self.place_in_area(matrix, 'A4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=64, object=matrix)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The outlier at B5 is too far right and lacks a spatial relationship with the main dataset, creating an unbalanced layout. Fix: Line 78: self.place_at_grid(outlier, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0) (line=78, object=outlier)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The dots grid is too low and occupies excessive vertical space, causing potential cutting at the bottom edge. Fix: Line 71: self.place_in_area(dots, 'D1', 'F3', scale_factor=0.6) (line=71, object=dots)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Labels are placed too close to dots, causing visual clutter and potential overlap with the dot labels. Fix: Line 66: self.place_at_grid(dim_label, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8); Line 67: self.place_at_grid(vol_label, 'C6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=66, object=dim_label, vol_label)
